title: Truncated universal nearby-cycle comparison and alteration geometry
statement:
For a finite commutative ring $\Lambda$, a scheme morphism $f:X\to S$, and $K\in D^b(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$, use the vanishing topos and ordinary comparison $\beta$ of [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. For $r\in\mathbf Z$, write $P_r(f,K)$ if for every $T\to S$ and every $T'\to T$ the cone of the ordinary comparison for $(f_T,K_T)$ and $T'\to T$ has $H^i=0$ for all $i\le r$. Thus the quantifier includes comparisons after an arbitrary preliminary base change, and does not merely truncate the comparison over $S$.

A modification of a reduced Noetherian scheme $S$ is a proper morphism $S'\to S$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] which is an isomorphism over a dense open $U\subset S$ and for which the inverse image of $U$ is dense in $S'$. An alteration is a proper surjective morphism, finite over a dense open of the target, all of whose irreducible components dominate irreducible components of the target. A semistable tower datum for this proof consists of an identity, or a finite tower of proper flat morphisms [def-weil-flat-morphism] whose geometric fibres are connected reduced curves with only ordinary double points, together with, for each factor, a chosen closed subscheme finite over its base [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] whose complement is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. At a geometric ordinary double point the completed local ring of the fibre is $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. An almost plurinodal datum here means a finite disjoint union of these semistable towers and a proper morphism with nowhere dense image. This is the proper tower data underlying the projective plurinodal morphisms supplied by the alteration theorem. Excellence of a scheme means excellence of every affine coordinate ring [def-exc-excellent-ring].
